flagRule: flagged = |seatA - seatB| > 15 over the two panel verdicts per answer (verified: 0 exceptions in 630 judged answers)
scoring: judgeScore = mean of the two seat scores; publishedScore = judgeWeight*judgeScore + (1-judgeWeight)*constraintScore where the item has constraintChecks (judgeWeight 0.5 or 0.7), else judgeScore. Seat scores are 100 minus deductions: critical -40, major -15, minor -5, floored at 0 (packages/runner/src/judge.ts at commit e3f8aee).

classificationDefinitions.ITEM-AMBIGUOUS: The prompt admits two defensible readings and the seats each took one; the item, not the judges, is the root cause.
classificationDefinitions.JUDGE-ERROR: One seat is wrong on a checkable fact — including lenient misses, where a seat scored high past a verifiable fault the other seat caught.
classificationDefinitions.SEVERITY-STACKING: The seats found the SAME fault(s) and priced them differently, or one seat counted a single root mistake as several findings — a compliance failure against the judge prompt's "each distinct underlying mistake exactly once" instruction.
classificationDefinitions.GENUINELY-BORDERLINE: A real judgement call (doctrine, severity of a marginal risk, edge-of-band arithmetic) where both readings are defensible.
classificationDefinitions.REFERENCE-SUSPECT: The item's own referenceAnswer/judgingNotes look wrong or contested; scores split along exactly that line.

reviewDepthDefinitions.deep: Question text and candidate answer (or the decisive part of it) read alongside both verdicts.
reviewDepthDefinitions.verdicts: Both seat verdicts (scores, findings, summaries) read; question context from the item file; answer text not independently re-read.

seatSeverity.note: Mean signed difference vs the colleague seat over all judged answers (95% normal CI). Severity is episodic, not a constant offset: unflagged answers agree to within 0.6 points on average in every pair.

The item's notes, not the answer, are wrong relative to the cited source.

grok-4.5 (95): "hard blues such as Stilton are explicitly allowed (NHS); only soft blues need avoiding."
